memory_candidates.content: When a shell test suite resolves its dependencies deploy-tree-first / source-store-fallback (the pattern used by scripts/tests/test-status-vocabulary.sh and its siblings), a mid-implementation local run can show a spurious FAIL if a *stale, pre-existing* deployed copy (e.g. .claude/context/schemas/state-schema.json from an earlier, unrelated deploy) predates the current source-store edit. This is not a defect in the new suite or the edit -- it resolves itself once the deploy step (usually the plan's own final phase) syncs the tree. Diagnose by comparing the source-store file directly against the deployed copy before assuming the new code is wrong; defer full-green confirmation to after deploy rather than fudging or skipping the check.

A negative-control demonstration for a fixture-driven shell test suite must invert the actual pass/fail LOGIC (e.g. drop the leading `!` on a `bash -n`/`jq empty` success check so valid input is counted as an error and invalid input is not), not just force a constant output. Forcing a constant (e.g. `errors=0` unconditionally) only flips the cases that were previously non-zero; it does not touch cases that already expected 0, so a 'both the failing fixture AND the clean control go [FAIL]' requirement (the correct demonstration that a probe's specific comparison logic, not just one branch, is exercised) is not satisfied by a constant-forcing mutation. Use a true sense-inversion instead.

Editing a JSON Schema file tracked in an extension's index-entries.json (which carries a hand-maintained line_count per entry) requires updating that entry's line_count alongside the content edit, or verify-deploy.sh's doc-lint Rule R will fail on the next deploy verification. generate-context-line-counts.sh --write exists to auto-correct this but rewrites every extension's index-entries.json in one pass with no per-file scoping flag -- for a single-file fix, hand-editing just the affected entry is safer and avoids pulling unrelated pre-existing line_count drift into an otherwise-narrow diff.
